summary:
Climora Safra
CLIMORA SAFRA was created by Team BMG for the NASA Space Apps Challenge – Cianorte (PR) Chapter. It uses climate data and NASA information to help farmers make safer decisions, reduce losses, and adapt to climate change.

The project’s persona is Grecco, a 20-year-old farmer who works with his family. Droughts, heavy rainfall, and frost threaten his productivity and income, so he needs reliable information to plan his activities.
The problem is that many farmers struggle to predict climate impacts on their properties. Water scarcity, erosion, soil depletion, and extreme weather increase risks, while choosing suitable crops for each region is complex.
As a solution, CLIMORA SAFRA is a web platform that analyzes rural properties using NASA data on temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, evaporation, heat stress, and water availability. It identifies unfavorable conditions, issues alerts, and estimates potential financial losses.
It also supports planning by highlighting periods of higher drought or frost risk and helping choose suitable crops, considering water conservation, erosion reduction, and soil quality.
Aimed mainly at small-scale farmers who depend on the weather, CLIMORA SAFRA turns NASA’s climate, soil, and water data into useful information, contributing to a more prepared, sustainable, and climate-resilient agriculture.
details:
What exactly does it do?

CLIMORA SAFRA is a web platform that analyzes the climate conditions of a rural property and identifies risks to production, such as drought, heavy rainfall, frost, and heat stress. It issues alerts, estimates potential financial losses, and helps farmers choose suitable crops. 

• How does it work?

The farmer enters the location of their property, and the platform retrieves NASA data on temperature, precipitation, soil moisture, evaporation, and water availability. It analyzes this data and presents simple alerts, risk indicators, and estimated losses. 

• What benefits does it have?

Safer planning of planting and harvesting.

Fewer production losses and financial damage.

Better crop choices for each region.

Support for sustainable practices such as water conservation and erosion reduction.

NASA data made accessible to small-scale farmers.

• What do you hope to achieve?

We hope to contribute to a more prepared, sustainable, and climate-resilient agriculture, helping farmers like Arthur protect their crops and income and better plan the future of their land. 

• What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?.

Languages: Vue JS, Typescript.

Software: Visual Studio Code, GitHub.

Hardware: Standard personal computers.
